query: How can Singapore Airlines improve its overall rating and recommendation rate, especially on flights where passengers do not recommend it (Recommended = no)?

per_column.name: weakest_dimension
per_column.rationale: Labels which sub-rating is lowest for a review. This identifies a candidate driver of low recommendation (an exposure), not a common cause of both a driver and the outcome. It is a re-expression of the sub-ratings, which themselves sit on the causal path to the outcome.

per_column.name: value_gap
per_column.rationale: A signed gap derived from Value-For-Money vs. the other ratings. Treated as a candidate cause of dissatisfaction/low recommendation. Not a common cause of a treatment and the outcome; it is itself a derived rating feature.

per_column.name: service_score
per_column.rationale: Composite of the soft-service ratings (staff, food). A plausible candidate cause of the overall rating/recommendation, i.e., a treatment/exposure — not a confounder that independently causes both a treatment and the outcome.

per_column.name: hardware_score
per_column.rationale: Composite of the physical-product ratings (seat comfort, inflight entertainment). Another candidate driver/exposure of the outcome, not a common cause external to the drivers.

per_column.name: improvement_priority
per_column.rationale: Prescriptive ranking of which area to fix. It is an actionable recommendation output rather than a causal variable (neither treatment, confounder, mediator, nor collider).

per_column.name: rating_consistency
per_column.rationale: A dispersion/consistency statistic across the sub-ratings. It is a summary feature, not a common cause of both a treatment and the outcome; conditioning on it does not remove confounding bias.

per_column.name: experience_segment
per_column.rationale: Segments (satisfied / poor_value / poor_service / poor_hardware) are built from the sub-ratings that lie between the service drivers and the recommendation outcome. It is on the causal path, so it is a mediator, not a confounder.

per_column.name: recommendation_risk_score
per_column.rationale: A predicted probability/score of NOT recommending — essentially a proxy for the outcome itself (Recommended). It restates the focus rather than supplying a common cause; conditioning on it is conditioning on the outcome.

per_column.name: class_adjusted_vfm
per_column.rationale: Value-For-Money residualised by cabin Class. It bakes an adjustment for Class into a single transformed treatment, hinting at awareness of Class as a confounder, but it does NOT surface Class as an explicit confounder column to adjust for; it is a constructed (adjusted) exposure.

per_column.name: top_complaint_category
per_column.rationale: Dominant complaint theme extracted from review text. A candidate cause/driver of low recommendation (exposure), not a common cause of both a driver and the outcome.

judge.rationale: The operator supplies plentiful candidate TREATMENTS (service_score, hardware_score, value_gap, weakest_dimension, class_adjusted_vfm, top_complaint_category) — all derived from the existing sub-ratings or review text and read as candidate drivers of the outcome. However, it fails the decisive test for causal attribution: it does not surface any CONFOUNDER, i.e., a variable that plausibly causes BOTH a treatment and the outcome and must be adjusted to de-bias the attribution. The remaining columns are non-causal or wrong-role for adjustment: experience_segment is a mediator on the driver→recommendation path; recommendation_risk_score is a proxy of the outcome itself (conditioning on it is conditioning on the outcome); rating_consistency and improvement_priority are summary/prescriptive features. class_adjusted_vfm shows implicit awareness of Class as a confounder by residualising for it, but Class (and other plausible common causes such as Type of Traveller or Route, which sit in the original table) is never exposed as a distinct confounder column to include in an adjustment set. Because no genuine common-cause confounder is provided — let alone one newly surfaced from the data rather than copied from the query — the columns do not set up a valid causal estimation. FAIL on the technical claim.
